synthesis:
Today's screen leans hard into defensive income and value: 4 of 10 picks are Utilities, 2 are Consumer Defensive, and average component tilts read Value 88.6, Yield 87.0, Momentum 87.6 — with Quality trailing at 63.1. Six of ten are European, and the composite range compresses from 79 to 100, meaning after Covestro's outlier 100, the rest of the book is a tight cluster of cheap, high-yield, momentum-confirmed names. This is a screen picking up capital rotating out of growth into rate-sensitive yield.

The clearest thread runs through the regulated utilities: EIX, ES, RED.MC, and ENG.MC all surface on Value + Yield, trading 8-17x earnings against sector medians of 22x while paying 4.2-6.0% versus a 3.2% median — the classic bond-proxy trade reasserting itself as US chip stocks log their worst week in over a year and mega-cap tech leadership rotates. A second thread ties EDEN.PA and KHC together on cash-yield: 14.8% and 10.5% FCF yields respectively, both with momentum in the 88-99th percentile.

The outlier is Covestro at rank 1 — the 100 composite is a takeover artifact from the ADNOC approach, not fundamentals (ROE -9.4%, FCF yield -4.2%). More telling is the absence: zero picks from Technology, Healthcare, Industrials, Energy, or Communication Services out of 680 scored names — concentration risk is real. Watch ADNOC-EU antitrust progress and any escalation of the Iran-linked fertilizer supply squeeze flagged by Germany's farm lobby, which reads directly onto OCI.
